assays.assay_description: Mice received s.c. 4-Br-DMT, psilocin, DMT (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle (with or without WAY100635 / SB242084 pretreatment) and were video-recorded in a test chamber for 30 min; HTR counts were quantified with a DeepLabCut pose-estimation model plus a SimBA classifier, with time-course and dose-response analyses.

application_type.evidence: mice received subcutaneous test drug (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle (saline or 90:5:5 saline:DMSO:Tween 80)

setup_habituation.evidence: Baseline temperature was recorded after brief chamber acclimation and compared to post-session body temperature readings

setup_restrain.evidence: behavior was video-recorded for 30 min ... Motor activity (distance traveled) was determined using the head pose-estimation key point (animals freely moving in chamber)

food_restriction.evidence: Not explicitly stated; 30-min recording in a test chamber with no food described

water_restriction.evidence: Not explicitly stated; 30-min recording in a test chamber with no water described

time_to_assay.evidence: mice received subcutaneous test drug (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle ... and behavior was video-recorded for 30 min

sample_size.evidence: All values are mean ± SEM for n = 5-6 mice, except for the 30 mg/kg dose of 4-Br-DMT (n = 1 due to lethality post-session, marked with X through the symbol).

outcomes.summary: 4-Br-DMT (0.03-30 mg/kg, s.c.) did not significantly increase head-twitch counts at any dose, whereas psilocin (0.3-10 mg/kg) and DMT (3-10 mg/kg) significantly increased HTRs vs vehicle over the first 10 min post-injection (ED50 = 0.15 and 2.24 mg/kg, respectively). Pretreatment with WAY100635 alone or combined with SB242084 did not unmask latent HTR activity of 4-Br-DMT.
outcomes.statistics: Group comparisons were made via Welch's ANOVA with Dunnett's T3 vs vehicle, alpha = 0.05; ED50 psilocin = 0.15 mg/kg, DMT = 2.24 mg/kg; HTR dose-response visualized with biphasic nonlinear fits.
outcomes.evidence: Relative to psilocin and DMT, 4-Br-DMT did not induce significant increases in the number of HTRs observed (Figure 5A-D). Conversely, psilocin and DMT induced increases in the HTR counts of mice treated with 0.3-10 mg/kg and 3-10 mg/kg relative to vehicle controls over the first 10 min post-injection.

assays.assay_name: Locomotor Activity (distance traveled in test chamber)
assays.assay_description: Total distance traveled (cm, % vehicle) measured over the same 30-min video-recorded session following s.c. 4-Br-DMT, psilocin, DMT (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle; determined from the DeepLabCut head pose-estimation key point, with four-parameter dose-response fits.

application_type.evidence: mice received subcutaneous test drug (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle (saline or 90:5:5 saline:DMSO:Tween 80)

setup_habituation.evidence: Baseline temperature was recorded after brief chamber acclimation

setup_restrain.evidence: Motor activity (distance traveled) was determined using the head pose-estimation key point (freely moving animal)

food_restriction.evidence: Not explicitly stated; 30-min recording in a test chamber with no food described

water_restriction.evidence: Not explicitly stated; 30-min recording in a test chamber with no water described

time_to_assay.evidence: acute drug effects were recorded for 30 min following injection

sample_size.evidence: All values are mean ± SEM for n = 5-6 mice, except for the 30 mg/kg dose of 4-Br-DMT (n = 1 due to lethality post-session).

outcomes.summary: All three tryptamines (4-Br-DMT, psilocin, DMT) reduced total distance traveled over the 30-min session at the highest doses tested (3-30 mg/kg), indicating hypolocomotion. At 30 mg/kg, 4-Br-DMT produced seizure-like activity and lethality (only one mouse tested at that dose).
outcomes.statistics: Four-parameter nonlinear fits for motor activity; group comparisons via Welch's ANOVA with Dunnett's T3 vs vehicle, alpha = 0.05.
outcomes.evidence: 4-Br-DMT, psilocin, and DMT all induced hypolocomotor effects (Figure 5E) and reduced body temperature (Figure 5F) at the highest doses tested (i.e., 3-30 mg/kg).

judge_notes: Candidate 'qwen' returned an empty assays list despite the paper containing in vivo mouse behaviour; its assay-level omission was overridden using the other two candidates and the paper text.

Retained two assays: HTR and locomotor distance. Although both were measured in the same 30-min session and chamber, they are different behavioural domains, which the rubric treats as separate assays.
Body-temperature change (Figure 5F) was NOT scored — purely physiological measure, excluded per rubric.
Radioligand binding and synaptosome monoamine transporter assays (ex vivo/in vitro) excluded.
Antagonist (WAY100635 / SB242084) HTR experiments were merged into the single HTR assay per the 'same test with added antagonists = 1 assay' rule.
B1 corrected to 0 for both assays (single behavioural measure each); gemma4 incorrectly assigned 1 point for a single measure.
D2 corrected to 1 (15–60 min) for both assays: the paper explicitly states 30-min recordings; gemma4's '<15 min' contradicted its own evidence quote.
B2: scored Yes for HTR (explicit time-course plots, Figure 5A-C and 'first 10 min post-injection' analysis) but No for locomotion (only total distance over the 30-min session reported).
doses_mg_per_kg left empty for the tryptamines: only the range '0.03-30 mg/kg' is stated in text, individual dose levels are not enumerated; gemma4's enumerated list was an inference and was dropped.
setup_habituation scored 'yes' (medium confidence) based on 'Baseline temperature was recorded after brief chamber acclimation', which indicates apparatus exposure before the recorded session.
